pages.text:
The controller's GUI has three pages: Plasma (its readings and trends), Plant (temperatures, wear, tanks, fuel cycle) and Control (setpoints and the start-up checklist).
# Start-up checklist
1. Vacuum: the Cryopumps pump the vessel to 10^-5 atm. One pump takes 30 seconds on the smallest vessel; bigger vessels take longer, more pumps less.
2. Cold: the coils below 20 K on Liquid Helium (85 K on Liquid Nitrogen alone). From warm, Liquid Helium takes about two and a half minutes.
3. Field: energised to the field setpoint.
4. Solenoid: the Central Solenoid charged with FE (not on a stellarator).
5. Heating: a Gyrotron or Neutral Beam Injector fitted and a heating setpoint.
6. Fuel: a Pellet Injector or Gas Puff Valve fitted.
Then press Run.

# Setpoints
- Heating (MW): shared among the Gyrotrons, then the Neutral Beam Injectors.
- Density: as a share of the Greenwald limit. Fuelling holds it there, the mix kept even, and thins it near the beta limit.
- Current: as a share of the most the field allows.
- Field: as a share of the full field.
- Fuel: D-T, or D-He3.
- Repeat: start the next pulse by itself when one ends.
# Control
Run in the GUI or the machine control API. Redstone: High runs it while there's a signal; Low runs it unless there is one. Fast Shutdown ends the plasma at once, cleanly; it doesn't disrupt.

# Pulses
A tokamak's pulse lasts as long as its solenoid's flux: about six minutes on the smallest. When it's spent the current ramps down and the plasma ends, and the solenoid recharges for the next.
# Power
Q is fusion power over heating power. On 50 MW of heating the smallest reactor runs at Q around 5 (about 270 MW); each size up makes more, to Q near 40 (about 2,000 MW) on the largest. Ignited means the alpha heating alone holds the plasma's temperature.
Each MW of fusion heat is 1,500 HU/t. The blanket takes the neutrons' share (80%, raised by lithium-6) as Hot Lead-Lithium for Steam Generators (High-Pressure Steam, for Nuclear Steam Turbines); the rest lands on the wall and divertor, carried off by Water as Hot Coolant.
# The helium loop
Fill the coolant tank with Helium instead of Water and the wall comes out as Hot Helium, 100 HU a mB, for Helium Gas Turbines; the gas also takes whatever blanket heat the Lead-Lithium can't, so the Lead-Lithium only needs to breed. A Helium Gas Turbine gets a little more from each HU (8 FE against steam's 6.7) and sends the Helium back. Drain one loop's fluid before switching to the other.

# D-He3
Switch the fuel to D-He3 with Helium-3 in the Pellet Injectors. It gives almost no neutrons: little activation, little wear on the blanket, no tritium to breed. It needs a large, hot plasma and plenty of heating: on 100 MW it burns from major radius 6 up (about 1,600 MW from the largest, with almost no neutrons), and smaller reactors can't hold it.
